questions.solution_text:
|3x - 2| = 16
$\text{Case 1: } 3x - 2 = 16 \implies 3x = 18 \implies x = 6$
$\text{Case 2: } 3x - 2 = -16 \implies 3x = -14 \implies x = -\frac{14}{3}$
$\text{Check } x = 6: \left|\frac{3(6) - 2}{4}\right| = \left|\frac{16}{4}\right| = 4 \text{ (valid)}$
$\text{Check } x = -\frac{14}{3}: \left|\frac{3(-14/3) - 2}{4}\right| = \left|\frac{-16}{4}\right| = 4 \text{ (valid)}$
$x = 6 \text{ or } x = -\frac{14}{3}$

questions.solution_text:
Multiply both sides by $3$: $|4x + 2| = 18$.
Case 1: $4x + 2 = 18 \implies 4x = 16 \implies x = 4$
Case 2: $4x + 2 = -18 \implies 4x = -20 \implies x = -5$
Check $x = 4$: $\left|\dfrac{4(4) + 2}{3}\right| = \left|\dfrac{18}{3}\right| = 6$, valid.
Check $x = -5$: $\left|\dfrac{4(-5) + 2}{3}\right| = \left|\dfrac{-18}{3}\right| = 6$, valid.
So $x = 4$ or $x = -5$.

$\text{Case 2: } 4x + 3 = -(2x - 1) \implies 4x + 3 = -2x + 1 \implies 6x = -2 \implies x = -\frac{1}{3}$
$\text{Check } x = -2: |4(-2) + 3| = 5 \text{ but } 2(-2) - 1 = -5 \implies 5 \ne -5 \text{ (extraneous)}$
